result.comment:
Story-004 retains its shared factory delivery design: save and push the tested change, create or reuse its PR, merge with the expected-head guard, confirm integration, then confirm issue closure. Feature-specific approval stays in the feature adapter; Bug uses the approved diagnosis and evidenced fixer success, with no second owner review.

This scoped architecture update resolves the earlier story-003 dependency. The owner has allowed local recovery checkpoints, and story-003 now supplies the canonical tested-content and validation binding. A checkpoint alone never starts delivery. Stale evidence parks finalization; an authorized reply resumes reconciliation before DOT may release fixer revalidation. Existing or uncertain remote effects remain attached across validation generations, preventing a second PR or merge. Confirmed valid integration proceeds only to remaining closure.

Source inspection also confirms that the existing harvest helper reads terminal text for its commit summary. The Bug save seam must instead use the accepted structured result. The retained main-race limit remains explicit: the API guards the PR head but cannot atomically guard main, so integration outside the validation binding stays unverified and cannot close the issue.

Only architecture changes. Story intent, guidance, dependencies and applicable prior decisions remain. No material question remains, and no tasks or criteria are authored. No implementation, executed tests, acceptance or publication is claimed. The complete Plan still requires its remaining factory-bound reviews before /implement <instruction>.

draft.name: Deliver successful fixes automatically

user_story.actor: An authorized owner of a reported bug
user_story.want: the factory to deliver the successfully validated repair and close the bug automatically
user_story.benefit: the approved fix reaches main without another review round, and an interruption does not lose progress or falsely mark the bug complete
notes: Assumption: delivery follows the existing shared factory policy for saving, pushing and merging, under repository permissions and protections.
Repair approval and the fixer's accepted success provide the agreed handoff; Bug adds no second owner review before merge.
Recovery applies to the simplified Bug flow. The owner will repost old bugs later; legacy execution migration and restart are outside scope.

draft.problem: A successful repair is not yet a delivered fix. Separate Bug delivery steps and another review round add work for the owner, while interrupted remote operations can leave it unclear whether the change was pushed, merged or the issue closed. Owners need the factory to finish delivery and confirm the result without repeating work that already succeeded.
in_scope: Begin automatic factory delivery from the fixer's accepted succeeded result for the approved repair, using its evidence of the exact tested code.

Have the factory save and push the tested change, create or reuse the repair PR, merge the fix, confirm integration into main and then close the bug issue. Completion requires confirmed integration and confirmed closure.
Reuse shared factory delivery capabilities without requiring Bug work to enter the feature or story lifecycle. Retain repository protections and existing publication permissions.

Deliver only the code covered by current validation evidence. When tested inputs change, require the prerequisite story's fixer revalidation before continuing delivery; do not introduce a separate factory validation run.
Retain delivery identities and status for the change, PR, merge and issue closure so interrupted work can continue from known progress across restarts.

Check remote state before repeating an operation whose outcome is uncertain. Reuse confirmed effects, avoid duplicate delivery and, once the fix is confirmed merged, perform only any remaining closure work.

Apply the common owner-question stop rule when delivery cannot continue, preserving the reason and known progress. An authorized reply resumes remaining delivery work without another repair approval or merge review.
not_in_scope: Diagnosing or repairing the bug, running the fixer's validation, or adding a factory test gate or repair loop.
A second Bug owner approval before merge or bypassing repository protections.
A new Bug-specific delivery subsystem, a general delivery platform rewrite or changes to unrelated feature and story policy.
Giving agents permission to push, merge or close issues themselves, or expanding existing permissions.
Migrating, restarting or reposting old Bug executions, removing legacy stores or runtime code, changing migration history or measuring code reduction.

general.decision: Factor the reusable save, PR, guarded merge and closure operations from existing delivery coordination. Bind them to one factory finalization activity for Bug; keep feature-specific admission in the existing feature adapter.
general.rationale: internal/turn/feature_delivery.go and internal/store/delivery.go require a managed feature generation, readiness and PR approval. Calling that flow unchanged would import excluded lifecycle requirements. internal/github/delivery.go already provides reusable remote primitives.

general.decision: Admit finalization only from the current approved diagnosis and its accepted succeeded fixer result, successful execution and complete current validation evidence. Create a factory-owned delivery authorization bound to those references and the tested content. Do not fabricate a PR approval or request another owner review.
general.rationale: The owner explicitly selected automatic delivery. Keep feature merge approval unchanged and document the narrow Bug policy difference from APP_CONSTRAINTS.md CONC-11 in the repository's amendment record when implemented.

general.decision: Compare actual saved and remote content with story-003's canonical tested source and relevant validation-input identities before publication and merge. Changed inputs require fixer revalidation; finalization neither runs tests nor performs an unvalidated repair or synchronization.
general.rationale: harvest.go currently commits and pushes in one helper. The reusable seam must allow checking the saved tree before push. A new commit identity alone preserves evidence only if it changes no declared validation input, as defined by story-003.

general.decision: Expose one finalization activity with completed, stale, owner-released revalidation and stopping outcomes. DOT owns every cross-activity transition and owner-resume behavior. Stale first parks; revalidation is available only after the claimed owner continuation and reconciliation. The activity's ordered remote operations remain a recoverable delivery transaction.
general.rationale: This retains story-002's loop/agent/finalization shape, story-001's common wait and story-003's resolved stale recovery contract. Do not copy the old pr/merge/close node graph, create a Go next-node map or add an automatic repair/test loop.

general.decision: Only the factory saves, pushes, creates PRs, merges and closes through existing git and forge gateways. Preserve repository protections, numeric identities, task ownership and explicit cancellation. Keep unrelated feature delivery semantics unchanged.
general.rationale: Existing agents have no forge credentials or delivery authority. Reuse does not authorize bypassing a required remote check or review, force-pushing, or mutating the registered clone checkout.

general.decision: Consume story-003's immutable delivery-eligibility binding: accepted result and successful execution, approved diagnosis, canonical tested content and validation inputs, target-main revision and passing evidence. Its owner-authorized local checkpoint is preservation only and never delivery authority; delivery starts after final succeeded.
general.rationale: The owner's Yes on issue 459 settled the checkpoint question. Story-003 now supplies the evidence and owner-released revalidation interface, replacing this story's earlier open assumption. No frontend design or legacy execution migration applies.

data_model.definition: An immutable graph-backed binding links task/repository and numeric issue identity, pinned graph, fixer attempt and accepted result revision, approved diagnosis/review, tested content and relevant validation-input identities, validation evidence, saved commit/tree, task branch and target-main revision.
data_model.constraints: Factory resolves identities from retained state and actual source observations. Agent fields cannot choose another issue, branch or authority. A changed validation generation gets a new binding linked to its predecessor; prior effects and remote object identities remain immutable history, not permission to duplicate a PR or merge.

data_model.definition: Retain save, push, PR creation/reuse, merge and closure operation identities with pending intent, dispatched, observed/refused/uncertain and confirmed facts in shared graph attempt records or their shared effect projection.
data_model.constraints: Use one authoritative record, not parallel Bug repair/check/delivery ledgers. Operation keys survive new resume attempts and bind exact effect inputs. Record intent before I/O and observations afterward. Compare-and-set claims prevent concurrent dispatch; do not hold a database transaction over I/O.

data_model.definition: Retain remote branch head, PR numeric ID/number, repository/branch/base and bot provenance, merge SHA and parent/integration observations, plus issue identity and confirmed closed state.
data_model.constraints: A successful HTTP response is not confirmation. A closed issue alone is not delivery proof. Completed requires confirmed integration of the authorized tested head into intended main and confirmed closure. Preserve contradictory observations rather than replacing them with success.

data_model.definition: Reuse story-001's durable origin wait, publication identity and consumed reply. Link the wait to the same delivery binding and outstanding effect, retaining any stale validation reason for story-003.
data_model.constraints: Owner guidance resumes finalization reconciliation once, not blind redispatch. Confirmed valid integration bypasses all repair, save, push and PR work; only remaining closure/report work may continue. A merged but unverified effect stays parked without another merge or automatic repair. Keep historical migration files; any shared persistence extension is a forward migration.

service_design.responsibility: Provide PR discovery/creation, guarded merge and observed closure with workflow-neutral inputs and a narrow factory authorization contract. Feature and Bug adapters supply their different admission checks.
service_design.access: Extract focused reusable operations from internal/turn/feature_delivery.go; retain existing internal/github/delivery.go methods and redacted mutation types. Do not pass a fake feature generation or approval comment into store.DeliveryProposal.

service_design.responsibility: Resolve and recheck the Bug binding, coordinate ordered effects, persist progress and return a declared outcome. Reuse the conservative observation rules in bug_merge.go and bug_close.go while removing their dependency on test-child and delivery-review records for the new flow.
service_design.access: internal/turn activity registry and internal/graphexec contracts, using graph persistence in internal/store. Dependencies are supplied by the factory, never role text. Consume only the accepted shared result; terminal text has no role.

service_design.responsibility: Reuse the local save and push mechanics through a seam that validates tested content before save, verifies the resulting tree before push and observes remote head afterward. Recover a completed local commit without committing it twice. Take commit and PR summaries from the accepted structured result, never terminal text.
service_design.access: internal/turn/harvest.go and internal/git, using story-003's shared local-save and canonical observation seams. Keep task ownership and CloneGate around local git critical sections, including observation and mutation. Existing ObserveBugRepair requires an already saved clean commit and cannot alone identify uncommitted tested input. harvest.go currently reads runResult.ResultText for the commit summary; Bug must replace that input with retained structured evidence.

service_design.responsibility: Store atomically retains binding, claims and observations; reporter publishes progress/questions through the existing journal; daemon schedules bounded reconciliation and owner continuations.
service_design.access: SQL remains in internal/store with its single connection and context-first calls. No sleeps or retry loops below daemon, no lock spanning an agent call, and no transaction spanning git or forge I/O. Use existing task coordination to exclude concurrent finalization.

solution_design.contract: Check current approval, accepted succeeded result, successful fixer execution and validation completeness. Observe tested inputs under task coordination. Save only the evidenced change, verify the saved tree equals the tested content and retain its commit identity. If save introduces changed content or unrelated unvalidated edits, stop before push. An earlier recovery checkpoint is not a successful handoff and must not activate the save/push path.
solution_design.rationale: This separates local save from publication and prevents success on one tree from authorizing another. Commit metadata changes can be recorded without pretending tests ran again only when no declared validation input changes.

solution_design.contract: Push through existing non-force policy and confirm the remote branch matches the retained saved commit. Find or create one factory-owned PR for the bound repository, branch and main. Correlate numeric identity, bot provenance and durable marker; ambiguous matches or a closed unmerged PR park. Recover uncertain creation by observation before any new create.
solution_design.rationale: ListDeliveryPRs includes closed and merged PRs, providing a reuse/recovery seam. Existing PR content rendering must describe Bug evidence and omit feature approval instructions and automatic issue-closing keywords.

solution_design.contract: Immediately before merge, recheck current evidence, PR/head/base identity, remote branch head and target-main revision. Dispatch the existing expected-head guarded merge only after durable claim. Independently observe PR merge facts and merge commit ancestry tying the tested head to intended main before allowing closure.
solution_design.rationale: MergeDeliveryPR guards the PR head, not the main revision. Preserve bug_merge.go's separate precheck and integration observations. Remote branch protection remains authoritative.

solution_design.contract: Treat an observed pre-merge target change as stale and require story-003 revalidation. The current API cannot atomically lock main with the merge request; inspect actual merge parents/content after dispatch. If a race produces integration outside the retained validation binding, record the merge fact, park and withhold closure rather than claiming verified delivery or attempting to merge again.
solution_design.rationale: A local lock cannot serialize external writers. This states the practical limit of the existing shared API without inventing an atomic base guard, bypassing protections or silently trusting stale evidence.

solution_design.contract: After confirmed authorized integration, observe the bound issue. Close it only if still open and its numeric identity matches, then independently confirm closure. If already closed after confirmed integration, record that observation without another mutation. Once completed, external reopening does not trigger automatic reclosure.
solution_design.rationale: Reuse CloseDeliveredParent and the stronger recovery discipline in bug_close.go. Issue closure must not stand in for integration proof or run ahead of it.

solution_design.contract: On every resume first load the existing delivery journal and observe uncertain effects. A timeout, lost reply or open PR does not prove nonexecution. Reuse confirmed effects; repeat a mutation only when authoritative observations establish it did not occur and its binding still permits it. If outcome stays uncertain, park through story-001. Preserve a successful local commit after push failure.
solution_design.rationale: This prevents duplicate PRs, repeated merges and premature closure across restart. A user reply grants continuation but cannot erase uncertainty or make stale evidence current.

solution_design.contract: Record stale evidence and park at finalization with its reason. An authorized reply resumes that origin once. Reconcile effects first; only when no merge has occurred or remains uncertain and revalidation is still required may finalization return the DOT-declared revalidation outcome. DOT then admits the fixer with current approval, stale reasons and a new validation generation under story-003. Finalization never dispatches the fixer directly. After the new succeeded result, reconcile the prior journal, reuse the existing PR and confirmed compatible effects, and bind any new effects to the new evidence. Confirmed valid integration resumes only remaining closure.
solution_design.rationale: Story-003 now defines this owner-released recovery path. No automatic finalization-to-fixer test loop or factory check is introduced. Revalidation does not erase old effects or authorize a second merge; uncertain or merged-but-unverified effects remain parked for reconciliation.
